title: 第17章 出口的代价第18章 深渊的回响
slug: 黯潮纪元异世界的崛起
lines: 审讯室的门关上时，锁舌咬合的声响比预想中更沉。
陈默坐在木椅上，指尖搭着膝盖。对面的人没有急着开口，而是慢条斯理地解开长袍领扣，露出里面白色衬衫的领口——浆洗得笔挺，连一丝褶皱都没有。
塞西尔·维拉，教廷特使。
他把一本薄薄的册子放在桌上，封面朝下。然后他笑了，那个笑容温和得像在教堂里分圣餐的神父。
“别紧张，陈默骑士。我只是想聊聊。”
陈默没说话。他的目光扫过房间——四壁白灰墙，没有窗户。唯一的光源是桌上那盏油灯，灯芯燃烧时偶尔爆出一朵灯花。空气里有股霉味，混着某种干燥的草药气息，像是艾草和薄荷的混合物。
“你加入骑士团多久了？”
“三周。”
“三周。”维拉重复了一遍，像在咀嚼这个词。“三周前，你还只是个见习骑士，连圣光都无法稳定引导。现在——”他摊开手，“你已经是正式编制的骑士，还在圣光失控事件中稳定了局面。”
他的手指在桌上轻轻敲了两下。
“进步很快。”
陈默感觉到后颈有细微的刺痛。不是伤口，是直觉。这个人在用赞美编织绳索。他把身体重心从右腿换到左腿，椅子的木腿在石地上刮出一声轻响。
“运气好而已。”
“谦虚了。”维拉翻开册子，里面夹着几页纸。陈默瞥见上面的字迹——不是骑士团的档案格式，是另一种更工整的字体。教廷自己的记录。
“你之前所在的圣殿骑士团第三分队，在一次边境巡逻中遭遇黯潮生物。全队覆没，只有你活了下来。”维拉抬起头，目光在陈默脸上停留了两秒。“那之后，你被判定为‘圣光感知不稳定’，调离原部队，转入后勤序列。”
陈默的呼吸没有变化。这些是雷诺·艾德伍德的履历，他已经背得滚瓜烂熟。
“然后你在银月城重新激活了圣光，加入了德文·铁卫的骑士小队，参与了圣光失控事件的处置。”维拉合上册子，看着陈默。“你的人生，像是在三周前重新开始的。”
房间里安静下来。油灯的火苗跳了一下，影子在墙上晃动。
陈默知道他在等什么——等一个破绽，一个眼神闪烁，一个吞咽动作。审讯的基本技巧。
他给了维拉最无聊的答案：“死过一次，很多事情就看开了。”
维拉盯着他看了五秒，然后笑了。那个笑容比刚才更真诚了一点，但陈默不确定这是好事。
“说得对。”维拉把册子推到一边，身体前倾，手肘撑在桌上。“那我直接问了——你在圣光失控的那天晚上，看到了什么？”
来了。
陈默的脑海中闪过那个画面：银月城大教堂的钟声，从三星堆青铜面具中听到过的声音。阿尔德里奇留在屋顶的螺旋符文，他的警告。
他选择说真话的一半。
“我看到圣光在扩散，像一张网。它在覆盖城市，但不是在保护，而是在...标记。”
维拉的眉毛动了动。“标记？”
“像在确认什么东西的位置。”陈默说，“我不知道那是什么，但我觉得圣光有自己的意志。”
这句话说出口的瞬间，陈默感觉到指尖传来一阵微弱的震动。不是来自椅子，不是来自地面——是来自他体内。
圣光在回应他。
维拉沉默了。他低头看着桌面，手指交握，拇指互相绕圈。那个动作很慢，很均匀，像在计算什么。
“圣光有意志。”他重复了一遍，声音很轻。“这个说法，在教廷内部，属于异端。”
陈默的心跳漏了一拍。
“但我不这么认为。”维拉抬起头，眼神里有一种陈默没预料到的东西——认真。“教廷的教典说圣光是神的恩赐，是纯粹的，是受圣徒意志引导的。但前线回来的骑士都知道，圣光有时候会自己动。”
他站起来，走到墙边。那里挂着一幅银月城的地图，维拉用手指在城区的某个位置点了一下。
“圣光失控的中心，是阿尔德里奇法师塔。”他转过头，“你认识阿尔德里奇吗？”
“见过一面。”
“他把自己关在塔里，已经三周了。教廷的人进不去，他的魔法屏障还在运转。”维拉转过身，背对着地图。“他在塔里做了什么，看到了什么，没人知道。但你——”
他走回桌前，俯视着陈默。
content_en:
When the door to the interrogation room closed, the sound of the lock bolt snapping was heavier than expected.
Chen Mo sat on a wooden chair, his fingertips resting on his knees. The person opposite did not speak in a hurry, but slowly unbuttoned the collar of his robe, revealing the collar of the white shirt underneath - it was starched and straight without even a trace of wrinkles.
Cecil Vera, Nuncio of the Holy See.
He placed a thin book on the table, cover face down. Then he smiled, a smile as gentle as a priest giving Holy Communion in church.
"Don't be nervous, Knight Chen Mo. I just want to chat."
Chen Mo said nothing. His eyes scanned the room—white and gray walls, no windows. The only source of light was the oil lamp on the table. When the wick burned, a flower occasionally popped out. There was a musty smell in the air, mixed with some dry herbal smell, like a mixture of wormwood and mint.
"How long have you been a member of the Order?"
"Three weeks."
"Three weeks." Vera repeated, as if chewing the word. "Three weeks ago, you were just a trainee knight, unable to even guide the Holy Light stably. Now -" he spread his hands, "you are already a formal knight, and you stabilized the situation when the Holy Light was out of control."
He tapped his fingers twice on the table.
"Progress is rapid."
Chen Mo felt a slight tingling sensation on the back of his neck. It’s not a wound, it’s a gut feeling. This person is weaving a rope with praise. He shifted his weight from his right leg to his left leg, and the wooden legs of the chair scraped softly on the stone ground.
"It's just good luck."
"I'm humble." Vera opened the booklet with a few pages inside. Chen Mo caught a glimpse of the handwriting on it - it was not the Knights' file format, but another neater font. The Holy See's own records.
"The third detachment of the Knights Templar that you were in encountered a dark tide creature during a border patrol. The whole team was wiped out, and only you survived." Vera raised her head and her eyes stayed on Chen Mo's face for two seconds. "After that, you were judged to have 'unstable Holy Light Perception' and were transferred out of the original unit and transferred to the logistics sequence."
Chen Mo's breathing did not change. These were Reno Edwood's resume, and he knew them by heart.
"Then you reactivated the Holy Light in Silver Moon City, joined Devin Iron Guard's knight team, and participated in the handling of the Holy Light out of control incident." Vera closed the book and looked at Chen Mo. "It's like your life started all over again three weeks ago."
The room fell silent. The flame of the oil lamp jumped, and the shadow swayed on the wall.
Chen Mo knew what he was waiting for - waiting for a flaw, a twinkle in his eyes, a swallowing movement. Basic interrogation techniques.
He gave Vera the most boring answer: "Once you die once, you can see away many things."
Vera stared at him for five seconds, then smiled. The smile was a little more sincere than before, but Chen Mo wasn't sure that was a good thing.
"That's right." Vera pushed the book aside, leaned forward, and rested her elbows on the table. "Then let me ask directly - what did you see that night when the Holy Light lost control?"
Coming.
That image flashed through Chen Mo's mind: the bells of the Silver Moon City Cathedral, the sound he had heard from the Sanxingdui Bronze Mask. Aldridge left a spiral rune on the roof, his warning.
He chose to tell half the truth.
"I saw the light spreading, like a net. It was covering the city, not protecting, but... marking."
Vera's eyebrows moved. "Mark?"
"It's like confirming the location of something." Chen Mo said, "I don't know what it is, but I think the Holy Light has its own will."
The moment these words were spoken, Chen Mo felt a faint vibration coming from his fingertips. Not from the chair, not from the ground—from inside him.
The Light was answering him.
Vera was silent. He looked down at the table, interlacing his fingers and circling his thumbs around each other. The movement was very slow and even, as if he was calculating something.
"The Holy Light has a will." He repeated, his voice very soft. "This statement is considered heretical within the Holy See."
Chen Mo's heart skipped a beat.
"But I don't think so." Vera raised her head, with something in her eyes that Chen Mo didn't expect - seriousness. "The Holy See's canon says that the Holy Light is a gift from God. It is pure and guided by the will of the saints. But the knights who have returned from the front line all know that the Holy Light sometimes moves on its own."
He stood up and walked to the wall. There was a map of Silvermoon City hanging there, and Vera clicked on a certain location in the city with her finger.
"The center of the out-of-control Holy Light is Aldridge's Mage Tower." He turned his head, "Do you know Aldridge?"
"I met him once."
"He has locked himself in the tower for three weeks. People from the Holy See can't get in, and his magic barrier is still running." Vera turned around and turned his back to the map. "What he did in the tower, what he saw, no one knows. But you—"
He walked back to the table and looked down at Chen Mo.
